players.product: QCT single-molecule NGS (smNGS) prenatal (UNITY) and oncology (Northstar) cell-free DNA tests with proprietary algorithms

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Oguzhan Atay on prenatal volume dynamics: test volume growth from single-specialty independent OBGYN clinics was very consistent in 2025 and 2026; lumpiness comes from health system additions, which are binary and bring anywhere between 3,000 to 5,000 tests each (3,000 to 5,000 tests per quarter), so one health system in a quarter can raise growth by almost 50%. The market is 40% independent clinics and 60% health systems; BillionToOne has about 20% market share, the vast majority in independent clinics, and most of the remaining opportunity is in health systems, which is why it invested in Epic Aura and the Excel panel (started more than a year ago to serve genetic counselors). In 2025 a single health system win in Q2 lifted growth to almost 15,000 tests in Q2 and Q3. Many health systems are already on board clinically, but EMR, legal sign-off and phlebotomy onboarding can take anywhere between six months to even 18 months; CEO: 'a matter of when rather than matter of if', and the difference between 2025 and 2026 is health-system onboarding timing, not really competition.
quarterly_data.figure: 3,000 to 5,000 tests per quarter per health system; market 40% independent clinics / 60% health systems; about 20% market share; almost 15,000 tests growth in Q2 and Q3 2025; onboarding six months to 18 months

quarterly_data.signal: CEO on 2026 guidance: it includes only what is completely under the company's control and very predictable, with no big health system wins, no true-up revenue and no new coverage decisions; 'We are going to be able to meet and exceed those targets', and the company would significantly exceed its expectations if a large health system is onboarded, significant true-up revenue comes in or an unplanned coverage decision arrives. The held claims involve a single large payer BillionToOne went in network with earlier in the year, under two additional agreements that contractually bind the payer to pay for the tests while the claims are held during its state-by-state code implementation; CEO calls it implementation timing rather than a reimbursement issue, says that in many of those states the payer previously was not paying for the vast majority of its tests (so significant incremental revenue and ASP), holds weekly meetings with it and says it is being resolved right now.

CEO on prenatal reimbursement and ASP: BillionToOne is now in network with close to 300 million lives. Its prenatal business has a 30-plus percent operating margin versus his estimate of 0%-10% operating margin for most businesses in the market, which he credits to declining low-rate contracts and to assays separated so each can be billed with its own code. It might get paid 70% of the time for carrier and aneuploidy but only 20% of the time for single gene NIPT and the 22q microdeletion; when first modeling, the company thought maximum ASPs would be around $375, $400 (what competitors achieved after years in the market) and it is already way beyond that. With coverage decisions across all its tests, even at those 70% numbers, prenatal ASP can easily be $800-plus; CEO: that will not happen in the next 12 months, but small drivers will keep increasing ASP.
quarterly_data.figure: close to 300 million lives in network; prenatal operating margin 30-plus percent; paid 70% of the time (carrier, aneuploidy) vs 20% (single gene NIPT, 22q microdeletion); potential $800-plus prenatal ASP

quarterly_data.signal: CEO on competition: competitors are launching products they previously dismissed, while in the past year BillionToOne expanded fetal antigen testing (which he says no other labs provide), launched Unity Confirm and expanded Fetal Risk Screen to 130 genes. The number of providers added each quarter is very similar to the past, and half of new providers came from one particular competitor in 2024 and 2025 and again in 2026, so he says competitive dynamics did not really change; the time-limiting step is EMR integration, logistics and phlebotomy rather than the clinical discussion. Unity Confirm interim readouts are expected in the first half of next year, and more evidence is needed before it alone drives switching. In prenatal, an awareness survey shows half of providers do not know about UNITY or BillionToOne after six, seven plus years in the market.
quarterly_data.figure: Unity Confirm interim readouts in the first half of next year; half of new providers from one competitor in 2024, 2025 and 2026; half of prenatal providers unaware of the company

quarterly_data.signal: CEO on oncology reimbursement: BillionToOne is contracted with most payers. Northstar Select has 60%-70% gross margins without an ADLT price; an ADLT price, about a 12 to 18 month process once the company decides to go through FDA approval or clearance (for a therapy selection test FDA clearance or approval is the only requirement), can literally triple Northstar Select's ASP. He would pursue FDA approval in the medium to long term but not immediately, because it locks the assay in and slows iteration. Northstar Select recently received additional coverage decisions from Lab Benefit Managers; Northstar Response turned gross margin positive without Medicare coverage, and coverage would bring both a much higher ASP and much higher utilization. In a new oncology territory it can take 3 months before a rep sees a first oncologist, after which referrals make adoption faster and faster.
quarterly_data.figure: Northstar Select 60%-70% gross margin without ADLT pricing; ADLT 12 to 18 month process; ADLT could raise Northstar Select ASP 3X; Northstar Response gross margin positive without coverage

quarterly_data.signal: CEO on MRD and response monitoring: response monitoring (late-stage cancers, a quantitative tumor-burden measurement) can be almost as large a market as MRD, with more frequent testing, and he does not think competitors can replicate Northstar Response's quantitative measurement. In MRD BillionToOne aims for a tumor-naive test on par with, or potentially better than, some tumor-informed tests; most MRD utilization today is in academic groups, about 20% of the overall market, while 80% is community oncologists, where ease of use is critical. Each product is designed to reach close to 80% gross margin at scale, with earlier high-margin products paying for newer products that lack coverage so growth need not be throttled.
quarterly_data.figure: academic about 20% / community oncology 80% of the market; close to 80% gross margin per product at scale
